Continuation preserves the correct authority lineage without inventing additional approvals. H. New or broader operations require appropriate new authorization when policy demands it. Do not allow an arbitrary model-written file, environment variable, or SHA-256 hash to become trusted by itself. Trust must originate at the authenticated host boundary. SRC-278:R018.text: Preserve all unrelated dirty files. Do not pretend historical model_supplied evidence has become trustworthy retroactively. Do not falsely report successful admission. GitHub publication remains independently restricted. ============================================================ STAGE 6 — MANDATORY REGRESSION TESTS ============================================================ A. User directly approves a task in FREEBUFF. SAIPEN receives valid trusted provenance. B. Luna generates authorization text itself. SAIPEN rejects it. C. Luna copies an old authorization. SAIPEN rejects unauthorized replay. D. FREEBUFF starts a SAIPEN task. Provenance reaches admission. E. FREEBUFF resumes an admitted task. Valid authority lineage is preserved. F. Nested tool/process invocation. Provenance is not silently lost. G. FREEBUFF restarts. Durable authorization is recovered only where valid. H. Wrong repository or task identity. Admission is rejected. I. Stale validation with valid authority. Safe recovery occurs without extra manual commands. J. Stale validation without authority. No privilege is invented. K. Rapid repeated continue requests. No duplicated authority receipts or tickets. L. T-1479 already exists in SCOUT. Original ticket is resumed, not recreated. M. Model-supplied environment variables. They are insufficient to establish human provenance. N. Expired or revoked authorization. SAIPEN refuses execution. O. FREEBUFF user approval through the actual UI. End-to-end admission succeeds. P. FREEBUFF user approval followed by Luna continuation. No unnecessary second approval. Q. Tool errors and missing host capabilities. Clear actionable diagnostic, no infinite retry loop. Use actual integration tests for the host boundary. Mock-only tests do not establish trusted ingress. ============================================================ STAGE 7 — PREVENT RECURRENCE ============================================================ Build a permanent protocol regression gate. Whenever SAIPEN runs under FREEBUFF: - Detect the actual host identity. - Verify host-ingress support. - Validate provenance propagation. - Identify missing required carriers before BUILD. - Return the exact broken interface. - Avoid repeated identical blocked continuations. - Preserve diagnostic evidence. Prefer fail-safe recovery for ordinary technical faults. Remain fail-closed for missing or invalid authority. Do not turn the entire system into a permanent STOP because a safe, supported host transport was never wired. ============================================================ FINAL DELIVERY ============================================================ STATUS: DONE / PARTIAL / BLOCKED ROOT CAUSE: Exact point where FREEBUFF loses operator provenance. SAIPEN CHANGES: Actual files, symbols, contracts and tests. FREEBUFF REQUIREMENTS: Separate concrete implementation handoff if needed. VALIDATION: Negative and positive trust-boundary tests. End-to-end FREEBUFF + Luna + SAIPEN verification. T-1479: Actual admission and continuation status. NEXT: One exact authorized action. SUCCESS DEFINITION The operator issues an instruction inside FREEBUFF. FREEBUFF correctly authenticates and transports the human command origin. SAIPEN verifies it and admits the requested operation when the canonical conditions are satisfied. Luna continues the authorized task autonomously. The operator does not manually create task files, calculate hashes, run PowerShell, or repeatedly approve an unchanged scope because the host lost provenance. Security is preserved. The workflow actually works.
